$comment: Authoritative attestation reference for the production publicai-gateway CVM. Fetched at runtime by the /proof page. composeHash was read back from the CVM's RTMR3 event log on 2026-09-06 and cross-checked against the Phala control-plane API; both report 0ff36048. Image digests are the linux/amd64 children of the cosign-signed proof-v34 index for sub2api (INDEX 3f473d75) built by publish-tee-images run 34006774643 from commit bd0ec2094; the attestor image is deliberately left at its proof-v20 pin (INDEX cef1d03d) because deploy/attestor was not touched, and repinning it would widen the attested surface for nothing. VERIFICATION SCOPE, stated plainly: composeHash, osImageHash, the image digests and the build commit were each read back from a live source, and composeHash was cross-checked against two independent ones. The cosign keyless signature was NOT verified locally for this release - the workflow performs the signing and its run succeeded, and anyone can verify certificate identity https://github.com/FiiLabs/sub2api/.github/workflows/publish-tee-images.yml@refs/heads/feat/two-sided-market plus the embedded githubWorkflowSha against the sourceCommit below, but this file does not claim it was done. This release is a backend code change and adds no migration. It fixes newer Claude models becoming unusable: the provider hands the request to the upstream while impersonating a specific Claude Code client version, and the upstream had begun refusing its newer models below a minimum client version. Two parts. First, the built-in impersonated version pin was raised to meet that minimum (proof-v33). Second, and the reason a version bump alone did not suffice: the version actually sent upstream comes from a per-account identity cached in Redis that only ever moves forward when a newer real client happens to pass through the account, so an account with no recent current-client traffic stayed pinned to the old version and kept being refused; the loader now raises any cached version below the built-in pin up to the pin on read, replacing only the version number and preserving the rest of the identity, so every account converges to a usable version without waiting on incoming traffic. Earlier in this line: proof-v32 (two distinct experiences for consumer and contributor over one shared account, plus an attach-time model-quota probe that rejects an account with no paid plan), proof-v31 (recompute one internal account's historical earnings to current parameters, a data migration, rehearsed against a restored copy of production), proof-v30 (built from an amended commit later removed from the branch, skipped), v29 (referral copy pricing), v28 (audience-specific films on the landing page, Fable 5.1 copy), v27 (footer contact rail), v26 (upstream sync through v0.1.185 and beyond, Claude Fable 5.1), v24 (pricing copy at 14 percent and a 50 percent revenue share), v23, v22, v21, v20, v19, v18, v17, v16/v15. osImageHash, appId and instanceId are unchanged; the deploy passed --no-dev-os explicitly, because phala deploy silently switches to a dev OS image when it detects a local SSH key and a dev OS would void the attestation, and the control plane confirms is_dev false after the rollout. No data change, so the rollback point is simply the previous image digest. This rollout completed in 94 seconds with no incident.
